answer: The Dynamic Resource Tax requires every active node to continuously solve unique, memory-hard cryptographic puzzles scaled inversely to the network's current activity tide. When an attacker spawns clones, the resulting computational load pushes CPU demand past the profitability nadir, forcing hardware rentals to outpace rewards on every extra thread. Each fraudulent identity thus consumes more electricity than it earns, turning a single hidden ember of profit into a systemic financial loss that drains the operator's capital.
